segments.text: "Welcome to 'Circuit Breaker', your daily dose of robotics news.
It's August 20th, 2026.
In a big move, NVIDIA's new edge AI chip is set to transform on-device robot control, while the global humanoid market continues to heat up with shipments exceeding 22,000 this year.
Meanwhile, Waymo is giving its Gemini AI a home in its Ojai vehicles.
That's just a snapshot of what's new in robotics today."
From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "Post-Train NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge for On-Device Robot Control,"
it appears that NVIDIA has successfully developed a new version of its Cosmos 3 model, specifically designed for on-device robot control.
The Cosmos 3 Edge is a 4B omnimodel that features a 2B NVIDIA Nemotron-based reasoner, pre-trained on the same physical-world data as its smaller counterparts, the Cosmos 3 Nano and Cosmos 3 Super.
This approach enables the model to share a common grounding in understanding how objects move and interact, allowing it to be smaller and more power-efficient.
The Cosmos 3 Edge has been evaluated in closed-loop simulation, achieving a 22.9% success rate across 120 language-conditioned manipulation tasks.
From Humanoids Daily, "Global Humanoid Shipments Surpass 22,000 in H1 2026 as AGIBOT Leads and Form-Factor Debates Intensify."
Global humanoid robot shipments have exceeded 22,000 units in the first half of 2026, with AGIBOT leading the market with 9,700 shipments, accounting for 43.1% of the total.
AGIBOT's dominance is followed by Unitree, which delivered 7,000 units, making up 31.1% of the market.
The top five vendors, including AGIBOT and Unitree, collectively controlled over 86% of the market share.
The market is driven by entertainment, performance, and data-collection research, with these segments accounting for over 60% of the deliveries.
This significant milestone indicates a growing trend in humanoid robot adoption, with key form-factor debates expected to intensify in the coming months.
From Google / Google AI (Keyword Blog), "Waymo is bringing Gemini into its custom Ojai vehicles."
This story reports that Waymo is integrating Gemini, an in-car AI assistant, into its bespoke Ojai vehicles, aiming to enhance the passenger experience.

Gemini, which can be controlled using voice commands, will enable riders to adjust cabin settings, gather information on nearby attractions, and access various features independently of the Waymo Driver.
According to the integration, Gemini will operate in a separate instance, allowing it to process voice commands and respond accordingly.
This integration is part of Waymo's ongoing effort to improve its autonomous ride-hailing services.
From MIT News - Robotics, "MIT engineers design a better controller for operating construction diggers,"

MIT engineers have designed a new, more intuitive controller for operating construction diggers, which utilizes a miniature excavator's arm and bucket to mimic the machine's movements, effectively eliminating the need for mental mapping.

The new interface, named the "World-Space Interface," pairs the mechanical arm with a virtual simulation of an excavator, allowing operators to physically operate the machine in a virtual environment.
This method was achieved through the integration of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and human-centered design principles.

Initial results show that novices using the WSI were equally proficient as experts from the start, contrasting with traditional joystick-based simulators that required novices to learn complex mental maps.
From Robotics & Automation News, "X Square Robot showcases full embodied AI portfolio at WRC 2026."

X Square Robot is presenting its full portfolio of embodied AI technologies at the World Robot Conference 2026 in Beijing, featuring applications in logistics automation, dexterous manipulation, household robotics, and AI training-data collection.
The company's WALL-B embodied AI foundation model, robotic hardware, manipulation technologies, and data infrastructure are on display at booth C107.

Demonstrations include a logistics system that processed 1,816 parcels with an accuracy of over 98 percent and a flower-arranging demo that tests the robot's ability to understand natural-language instructions and perform complex manipulation tasks.
The company's showcased technologies are designed to enable more efficient and human-like robotic interactions.
From Humanoids Daily, "From Marathons to the Factory Floor: Beijing’s World Humanoid Robot Games Pivot to Real-World Utility".

The second World Humanoid Robot Games (WHRG) is set to kick off on August 22 in Beijing, with 2,056 robots from 666 teams across 16 countries participating in a shift towards commercial utility, introducing 21 scenario-based events that test robots in simulated factory, hotel, and retail environments.
The event has undergone significant changes, with task time limits slashed and remote-controlled operations facing severe scoring penalties.
This is done to test whether humanoid robots can perform reliable, autonomous work to generate economic value.
The tournament organizers have also strengthened autonomy rules, aiming to assess robots' ability to adapt to changing situations and tasks.
The new events and rules will push robots to navigate complex scenarios, such as assembling products, delivering packages, and interacting with customers.
By evaluating robots' performance in these simulated environments, the event aims to inform real-world applications and deployments.
The WHRG 2023 will pave the way for the adoption of humanoid robots in various industries, from manufacturing to service sectors.
Its focus on commercial utility and real-world scenarios will help accelerate the development of more practical and efficient robots.
The event's findings and insights will provide valuable insights for researchers, manufacturers, and businesses looking to integrate humanoid robots into their operations.
From Robotics & Automation News, "How Automated T-Shirt Printing Machines Are Transforming Textile Production".
This story highlights how automated T-shirt printing machines are increasing the speed and efficiency of textile production, allowing businesses to print more shirts in less time.
Automated T-shirt printing machines are being widely adopted by textile companies, with several manufacturers reporting significant improvements in print quality and reduced production costs.

These machines use advanced technology to quickly print various designs onto shirts, including company logos, pictures, names, numbers, and colorful designs, producing clear, vibrant, and neat prints.
The process involves loading the shirts and design onto the machine, which then uses inkjet or screen printing technology to apply the desired design.
By automating this process, companies are able to reduce manual work, minimize errors, and lower their production costs.
As a result, textile production is becoming faster, more efficient, and more cost-effective.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROSCon Global: regular price ticket sales end Monday + official after-hours events!"
Regular price ticket sales for ROSCon Global are set to conclude on Monday, August 24, 2026, at 12:00 AM UTC, marking the end of a limited opportunity for general registration.

The event's organizers have announced that after-hours activities, including an OSRF hackathon and a bus tour, will be made available at a later date, with registration required for participation due to limited space.
These exclusive events will offer attendees unique experiences and networking opportunities with industry experts.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS 2 Inspector — Static Architecture Analysis and Visualization for ROS 2 Workspaces,"

ROS 2 Inspector is a tool designed to automate the architectural pass for ROS 2 workspaces, utilizing static analysis to provide a compact summary of discovered ROS 2 packages and their health signals.
The tool generates interactive visualizations, offering data export in table, JSON, or YAML formats.
ROS 2 Inspector was developed to assist developers in comprehensively understanding the architecture of ROS 2 workspaces, providing a foundation for more efficient and effective development.
By leveraging static analysis, ROS 2 Inspector delivers a detailed analysis of ROS 2 packages, enabling users to identify and address potential issues before runtime.
This marks a significant advancement in static analysis capabilities for ROS 2 workspaces.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: VirtuLayer - A GUI for Nav2 Virtual Layer Plugin."

A web-based GUI called VirtuLayer has been developed to simplify the configuration and usage of the Nav2 Virtual Layer Plugin, allowing users to create virtual geometries on a map and generate the required configuration.
The plugin, which can be used to add virtual geometries to the Nav2 costmap, enables a simple visual workflow for creating and experimenting with virtual layers.
By providing a visual interface, VirtuLayer simplifies the process of configuring and using the Nav2 Virtual Layer Plugin, making it more accessible to users.
The development of VirtuLayer marks a significant improvement in the usability of the Nav2 Virtual Layer Plugin.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: A runtime that sits between an LLM and physical actuation - Does this fit your use case?"
This story reports on the development of a runtime called xZane, a runtime that validates commands against device capabilities before execution, and runs independently of the LLM.
The researcher has tested the xZane runtime on various devices, including a mobile robot, LG webOS TV, and robot vacuum, with similar results across different models and environments.
The xZane runtime differs from related work, such as ROSClaw and URML, by integrating a device's existing safety function and avoiding the safety-critical path of the model.
The researcher is now seeking feedback from others to determine if the approach fits their use cases, allowing the xZane runtime to be adapted for a broader range of applications.
"Thanks for coding with us on this robotic adventure!
Don't be a robot, stay curious!
Until tomorrow's charge, keep innovating and remember: in a world of wires, we're the ones who spark the future!
Goodnight, and may your circuits stay charged!"
